cells.tense: You stand at the full stretch of what you know with the pen still in hand.
cells.act: declare the shape of it outward, plainly
cells.ask: Say plainly, aloud or on paper, what shape the thing you've already worked out makes. Name what you see without hedging. Then step back and leave the sentence where it sits.
cells.core:
You can hold a great deal at once and still say what you see. Nothing you've gathered argues with anything else you've gathered; it all sits level and you can read it. What comes out when you speak from there is clear, and people build on it, because the ground doesn't shift under what you said.

The place you're standing is where things stop gathering and start needing to leave your hands. The work isn't more perceiving. Take something you've already worked out, say plainly what it is and what it means, and stop short of the next qualification. You'll feel the pull to keep qualifying. Let that go unsaid once and see whether the sentence still holds.
cells.sheetLine: You can hold all of it and still say what's true.
cells.verb: holding many truths at once and letting them land without argument
cells.place: the point where what has been gathered is complete enough to be released

cells.tense: You will be rehearsing every version of what comes next before any of it arrives.
cells.act: choose which star to steer by and steer
cells.ask: Pick one direction you actually want, from wanting rather than from what could go wrong, and head that way for three days. No surveying the alternatives in between.
cells.core:
When this runs hot, gathering turns into pre-running. A choice opens into several possible futures and you track them all at once, ahead of where you stand. The breadth that usually serves you becomes a survey you can't set down, and the next real thing you could do waits behind outcomes you've already imagined wrong.

What settles it isn't more seeing; it's a heading. Choose the light you'd steer toward if you weren't cataloguing what each route might cost, and go for three days without checking the other roads. What you find that way the survey could not have told you: what a whole day looks like when you stop watching every version of it at once.
cells.sheetLine: You're futures-reading everything and standing still.
cells.verb: holding many truths at once and letting them land without argument
cells.place: the point where what has been gathered is complete enough to be released

cells.tense: You were at a door that closed behind you and you did not turn around.
cells.act: join someone in the work so the two streams run as one
cells.ask: Bring what you're holding to a person working on the same thing and join the effort so it runs as two rather than one. Not to explain — to build it together.
cells.core:
Perceiving is still here; the movement has gone. You've been standing at the edge of something finished and calling it unfinished, when what it wants is to leave your hands and meet other hands. The gathering is done. The sending hasn't started, and standing here longer won't start it.

You don't have to push yourself back into it alone. Bring what you've gathered to somebody already working on the same thing and join your effort to theirs. Two streams running as one move further than one stream pushing by itself. The drag lifts when there's a second person in the water. What you finished really is finished; it just needs another hand to help it leave.
cells.sheetLine: Gathering is done and sending hasn't started.

cells.tense: You read the room accurately and do not count yourself as the one reading it.
cells.act: act on the private sense of what is right
cells.ask: Next time you see what's unfair near you, act on your own sense of what's right without waiting for permission or a second opinion. Do the small fair thing, then go on about your day.
cells.core:
You read situations fast and accurately — who's being left out, what isn't fair, what's owed. And you do it while telling yourself you're not sure. The perception arrives; you've just been keeping your name off it, as though somebody else put it there.

You don't need permission to act on what you already see. Next time something's unfair near you, do the small fair thing your sense already voted for, then go on about your day. Let the compass read clearly and follow it once without asking whether you were sure. The reply you get is what the action turns out to be, not the confidence you brought to it.
cells.sheetLine: You read the room and keep your name off the reading.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person's many knowings are 'still being weighed' at Too Much and 'waiting for acknowledgement' at Too Little — the record doesn't say they experience it as weight or waiting, I inferred it. A reasonable reader might say the Too Much read makes them sound paralyzed when they may simply be fast and thorough; the ask survives that because steering by one star for three days teaches what holding many truths costs, even for someone who isn't stuck. The sentence that serves me more than them is the Too Much sheetLine's 'forest of futures' image — I cut it. In the Balanced cell, 'clear about what you know' risks overstating; narrowed to what they actually do when they name a thing plainly.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person experiences the abundance as weight or as waiting — the record names fullness of perception, not how it feels from inside; my drafts keep smuggling in an inner weather report. A reader could object that Too Much makes them sound stalled when they may simply be fast and thorough, and Too Little makes them sound stuck at a finished thing when nothing says it is finished. The asks survive either error because each teaches something on its own terms — one heading shows what holding many truths costs, joining someone shows what gathering alone cannot finish. The sentence that served me more than them was the compass closing line in status 4, which flattered the reader rather than offering anything usable.
